text: A rain gauge is pretty simple. It's just a funnel catching rain. The top is wider than the inner measuring tube. That's the whole design. It's a magnification. If the top is ten times the area of the tube, one inch of rain falls in, it fills the tube ten inches high. And now you can read hundredths of an inch really easily and precisely. And then you can read very small amounts of rainfall. But you can introduce errors. Evaporation is one. It can evaporate pretty fast. And then you're not measuring the actual rainfall, you're measuring the rainfall that didn't evaporate. Then you have wind. Strong winds blowing around the mouth of the gauge.
